input.question: Let A be a subset of the positive integers, and for an increasing function ϕ: N -> (0, ∞) with ϕ(n) -> ∞, define the weighted upper density by d̄_ϕ(A) = lim sup |A ∩ [1, n]| / ϕ(n). If d̄_{n/ln n}(A) > 0, must the harmonic subseries sum_{n in A} 1/n diverge? More generally, does the same conclusion hold for weights of the form n/[(ln n)(ln ln n)...(ln^(k) n)]?

rewritten_question: Let A be a set of positive integers. For any increasing function ϕ: N → (0, ∞) with ϕ(n) → ∞, define the ϕ-weighted upper density of A by lim sup as n → ∞ of |A ∩ [1, n]| / ϕ(n). If this weighted upper density is positive for ϕ(n) = n/log n, must the harmonic subseries indexed by A, namely Σ_{n∈A} 1/n, diverge? More generally, for a fixed k, if ϕ(n) = n divided by log n, log log n, ..., and the k-th iterated natural logarithm of n (for all sufficiently large n), does positive ϕ-weighted upper density still force the subseries Σ_{n∈A} 1/n to diverge?

paper_evidence.quote: Problem 3. Given an increasing function ϕ : N →(0, ∞) with limn→∞ ϕ(n) = ∞, we define the upper density of weight ϕ by the formula ¯dϕ(A) = lim sup n→∞ |A ∩ [1, n]| / ϕ(n).
Does every subset A ⊂ N with ¯dn/ ln n(A) > 0 generate a divergent subseries P n∈A 1/n of the harmonic series?
What about the case of other weights n/[(ln n) (ln ln n)· · ·(ln ln · · · ln n | {z } k times )]?
Corollary 2. If (an)n is a sequence of positive numbers whose integer parts form a set of positive upper density, then the series P 1/an is divergent.
